specific_objectives: 6.1.3.1 Trainee will be able to perform rectification of corrosion.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of corrosion removal using pickling paste and wire brushing on simulated engine component samples; Safety precautions include wearing gloves, goggles, and ensuring ventilation; Instructor supervision required during chemical handling.
intro_questions: What are the primary causes of corrosion in aircraft engines?
List three common types of corrosion found on engine components.
Why is immediate rectification of corrosion critical for engine safety?

topics: Identification of corrosion types on engine parts
Preparation of surface for corrosion removal
Inspection of treated surfaces for defects
development.content:
Identification of corrosion types on engine parts
Preparation of surface for corrosion removal
Application of pickling paste technique
Mechanical removal using wire brushes
Inspection of treated surfaces for defects

topics: Neutralization and cleaning of treated areas
development.content:
Neutralization and cleaning of treated areas
Application of protective coatings
Final inspection and documentation
Safety protocols during chemical use
Proper disposal of waste materials

Review of rectification procedures
Common errors in corrosion treatment
Maintenance schedules for corrosion prevention
Reporting requirements for corrosion findings
Integration with overall engine maintenance

summary_questions: Explain the step-by-step process for rectifying corrosion on an engine component.
Describe the safety measures required when handling pickling paste.
How do you verify that corrosion has been completely removed?
